proposal.title: Braxiloosk: an export and import tool for social media archives
proposal.summary: Braxiloosk builds an export and import tool for social media archives for users of social platforms.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: People cannot move their posts and contacts between services. Users of social platforms depend on data portability every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build an export and import tool for social media archives called Braxiloosk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Data portability is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/braxiloosk/braxiloosk, which 172 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on data portability for 11 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the MIT licence in http://forge.test/braxiloosk/braxiloosk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 40800.00 EUR for 81 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 600.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
People cannot move their posts and contacts between services. Users of social platforms depend on data portability every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build an export and import tool for social media archives called Braxiloosk. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Data portability is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/braxiloosk/braxiloosk, which 172 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on data portability for 11 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the MIT licence in http://forge.test/braxiloosk/braxiloosk. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 7 months in 3 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 3. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 7.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 40800.00 EUR for 81 days of work over 3 tasks. Day rates range from 450.00 EUR to 600.00 EUR.
